claims.claim_text: The indexed Page R. Broadwater is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The full name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and official Army-entry file; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact private identifier and exact normalized full name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army-entry record is dated March 10, 1942; the index documents an OSS personnel file but not the OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The official merged file supplies one exact private-identifier and full-name match. Other Broadwater candidates were rejected.

claims.claim_text: Page R. Broadwater's Army-entry record places his civilian occupation in NARA's general-farm-hand category.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The fixed-width Army record carries occupation code 316, which NARA's official code table defines as farm hands on general farms.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed through the exact private identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded at Army entry on March 10, 1942, but no farm, employer, ownership status, location, or OSS transfer date is documented.
claims.match_notes: The historical occupation code is not converted into a named farm, employer, self-employment claim, or immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed French Second Lieutenant Hubert P. Brochard is a high-confidence match to BCRA officer Hubert Paul Brochard, alias Maurice Montjean, of the OSS-linked Sussex Cure mission.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The French military-archive finding aid identifies Hubert Paul Brochard and alias Maurice Montjean; an independent mission compilation places that alias on the OSS-linked Sussex Cure mission.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact uncommon first name, surname, middle initial expansion, French status, officer rank, archival alias, and OSS-linked Sussex mission context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The mission compilation places Brochard in France on June 1, 1944; the reviewed sources do not provide a direct Box 81 personnel-file identifier or pre-OSS employment chronology.
claims.match_notes: No direct Box 81 linkage was found, so the identity remains high confidence rather than confirmed. The wartime assignment is not repurposed as a pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Raymond J. Brochu is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The full name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and official Army-entry file; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact private identifier and exact normalized full name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The matching Army-entry record is dated April 21, 1943; another exact-name Army record with a different identifier is explicitly rejected.
claims.match_notes: The private identifier distinguishes the indexed person from a second exact-name Army entrant.

claims.claim_text: Raymond J. Brochu's Army-entry record places his civilian occupation in a semiskilled textile-manufacturing category not elsewhere classified.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Occupations in manufacture of textiles, n.e.c.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The fixed-width Army record carries occupation code 619; NARA's table assigns the 6 prefix to semiskilled work and group 19 to textile manufacturing not elsewhere classified.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed through the exact private identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded at Army entry on April 21, 1943, but no employer, mill, textile product, exact trade, or OSS transfer date is documented.
claims.match_notes: The composite historical code is described at its supported level and is not converted into a precise trade or named employer.
